primary.title: Household and similar electrical appliances - Safety - Part 2: Particular requirements for electric irons
primary.summary: IS 302-2-3 is the safety standard for mains-operated electric irons (dry and steam) for household and similar use. It is applied together with the general standard IS 302 (Part 1). It covers protection against electric shock, heating and temperature rise, moisture resistance, mechanical strength of the soleplate and cord, thermal cut-outs and endurance.

related.title: Household and similar electrical appliances - Safety - Part 1: General requirements
related.relation: Parent general-safety standard; every IS 302-2-x particular standard is read with Part 1.

related.title: PVC insulated flexible cords and cables
related.relation: Applies to the supply cord fitted to the iron.

related.title: Plugs and socket-outlets of rated voltage up to and including 250 V and rated current up to and including 16 A
related.relation: Applies to the plug fitted to the appliance.

certification.summary: Electric irons are under compulsory BIS certification. A manufacturer must hold a valid BIS licence and mark every iron with the Standard Mark (ISI mark with the CM/L number) before it can be manufactured, imported, stored for sale or sold in India. Selling unmarked or non-conforming product is an offence under the BIS Act, 2016.

qco.title: Safety of Household, Commercial and Similar Electrical Appliances (Quality Control) Order, 2024 (electric irons were first notified under the Electrical Appliances QCO, 2023)
qco.ministry: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
qco.enforced: As per the dates in the Quality Control Order / its amendments
qco.gazette: Published in the Gazette of India

sources.doc: Electrical appliance for commercial dispensing and vending QCO 2023 (gazette, same appliance family)

applicable.name: Scheme I (ISI Mark Scheme)
applicable.covers: Grant of a licence to use the Standard Mark (ISI mark) on electric irons after assessment of the manufacturing unit and testing of samples against IS 302-2-3 read with IS 302 (Part 1).
applicable.why: Household electrical appliances placed under a Quality Control Order require full ISI-mark certification with a factory Scheme of Inspection and Testing - not self-declaration.
applicable.you_receive: A BIS licence with a CM/L number and the right to affix the ISI mark on each iron; the licence is normally granted for 2 years and is renewable.

not_applicable.name: Scheme II (Compulsory Registration Scheme / CRS)
not_applicable.why: CRS covers electronics and IT goods notified by MeitY on the basis of a registration and self-declaration. Electric irons are household electrical appliances under Scheme I, not CRS.

not_applicable.name: Scheme X
not_applicable.why: Scheme X is for specified machinery/equipment built to a purchaser's specification; it does not apply to a mass-produced household iron.

sources.doc: Specific guidelines for Scheme-I (grouping guidelines) - BIS

testing.summary: Type testing is done on samples drawn from the factory, in a BIS-recognised laboratory (or the BIS lab), against IS 302-2-3 with IS 302 (Part 1). The factory must also run routine and acceptance tests under its Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT).

tests.name: Protection against electric shock / accessibility of live parts
Heating / temperature rise of handle, soleplate and surroundings
Leakage current and electric strength at operating temperature
Stability and mechanical hazards; cord anchorage and flexing
Resistance to heat, fire and tracking of insulating material
High-voltage (dielectric strength) test on every unit

sources.doc: BIS Product Manual for IS 302-2-3 - testing and SIT

labs.note: Testing must be done in a BIS laboratory or a BIS-recognised laboratory with IS 302-2-3 in its recognised scope. Use the BIS LIMS directory to find one and confirm scope and validity before sending samples.

licensing.summary: Scheme I (ISI mark) licence for electric irons is applied for online on the BIS Manak Online portal. The process is: apply and pay -> BIS records verification -> factory inspection and sample draw -> testing against IS 302-2-3 -> grant of licence with the CM/L number.

steps.title: Prepare and apply online
steps.detail: Create a firm account on Manak Online (manakonline.in), fill the Scheme I application for IS 302-2-3, upload the required documents, nominate the in-house testing facility and the Scheme of Inspection and Testing, and pay the application fee.

steps.title: Application scrutiny and recording of factory details
steps.detail: BIS scrutinises the application, the manufacturing process, machinery list and test facilities; raises queries if any.
steps.timeline: About 15-30 days after a complete application

steps.title: Factory inspection and sample drawal
steps.detail: A BIS officer visits the unit, verifies manufacturing and testing capability, witnesses in-house tests and draws sealed samples for independent testing.

steps.title: Independent testing
steps.detail: Samples are tested at a BIS / BIS-recognised laboratory against IS 302-2-3 read with IS 302 (Part 1).
steps.timeline: Depends on lab queue; typically a few weeks

steps.title: Grant of licence
steps.detail: On a satisfactory inspection report and passing test report, BIS grants the licence and CM/L number; the ISI mark may then be affixed. Licence is normally valid for 2 years and renewable.
steps.timeline: Overall, commonly around 4 months from a clean application; longer if there are test failures or query loops

sources.doc: BIS Product Certification - process and Scheme I guidelines

documents.summary: Documents to prepare for the Scheme I application for electric irons. Exact list is on the application form and the product manual; conditional items depend on the firm's constitution and location.

items.name: Proof of establishment of the firm / factory
items.explanation: Registration certificate, GST registration, factory licence or Udyam / MSME registration, and proof of the factory address.

items.name: Manufacturing process flow chart and list of plant and machinery
items.explanation: Shows the firm can manufacture the iron in-house, from sub-assembly to final assembly and packing.

items.name: List of test equipment with calibration certificates
items.explanation: The in-house lab must have the equipment to run the routine and acceptance tests in the SIT (e.g. HV tester, earth continuity tester, power meter).

sources.doc: BIS Product Manual for IS 302-2-3 - SIT

items.name: Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT)
items.explanation: The firm's documented plan of raw-material, in-process, routine and acceptance tests with frequency and records.

items.name: Test report of the product (if available) against IS 302-2-3
items.explanation: An in-house or third-party test report supports the application; independent BIS testing is still done.

items.name: Authorised signatory / board resolution and ID proof
items.explanation: Authorisation of the person signing the application on behalf of the firm.

items.name: Trademark registration / brand ownership proof
items.explanation: Needed if the iron carries a brand name owned by the applicant or used under licence.

items.name: For importers: Authorised Indian Representative (AIR) documents
items.explanation: A foreign manufacturer applies through an AIR with the AIR appointment and undertaking.
